title: Reshape a positioning-servo root locus
physicalPurpose: Meet simultaneous position damping, settling, accuracy, and drive-current requirements by changing controller structure.
objective: Prove why proportional gain alone fails and design and validate one lead compensator from explicit pole requirements.

simplifications: Ideal current actuation within declared limits

baseline.limitation: After root-locus breakaway, proportional gain changes frequency and damping but cannot move the pole-pair real part left of minus one.

change.decision: Accept only when complete-transfer-function poles and executable response meet overshoot, settling, final-error, and current constraints.

acceptance.window: 0 through 8 s after the one-millimetre step
first permanent entry into 0.98 through 1.02 mm

abortPredicates: Any required signal is missing, stale, forced, nonfinite, or has bad quality
Requested or applied motor current reaches its declared limit
Carriage position leaves the local five-millimetre range
Model, controller, timing, event, limit, or seed differs from the reviewed comparison
safety.restorationMode: Disable the experiment, command zero current, reset the lead state, and restart both simulated servos from zero position
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised motion-controls engineer and responsible machine operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: This lesson cannot authorise physical servo gain application
Physical validation requires independent mechanics, drive, topology, model, limits, interlocks, rollback, and explicit immediate approval

video.viewerOutcome: Explain why gain alone fails and design and validate a lead compensator from the complete root-locus response.

learning.context: Equivalent simulated positioning servos compare proportional gain with one calculated lead compensator.
learning.reason: Routh proves stability but does not reveal pole motion or whether a stable gain meets damping and speed requirements.
theory: Root-locus branches show closed-loop pole paths as scalar gain changes.
Damping lines and dominant poles connect pole location to response requirements.
A lead zero and farther-left pole reshape the angle condition.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict proportional poles and response, then calculate the complete lead polynomial, roots, zero effect, current, overshoot, and settling before running.
practicalPreparation: Verify equivalent plants, initial state, setpoint, units, timing, quality, limits, aborts, and Simulation evidence.
Record pole and response acceptance criteria before testing.
learning.baseline: Proportional gain four predicts about 16-percent overshoot and four-second settling.
learning.change: Implement lead compensation with gain 50, zero 2.5 per second, and pole 15 per second.
learning.comparison: Change only controller structure and derived parameters under equivalent conditions.
learning.validation: Require roots and complete executable response to meet overshoot, settling, accuracy, and current criteria.
learning.explanation: The lead pole and zero move the dominant branches left; the complete closed-loop zero explains the remaining difference from a second-order approximation.
learning.transfer: Root locus does not expose full-spectrum resonance and margins; Lesson 47 introduces Bode analysis.
